column4: This is the very top of everything. All other folders live inside this one, like the trunk of a tree.
column5: It's like the main gate of a house. Everything else is inside it.

column4: Personal folder for each user. Your documents, downloads, and desktop files are stored here.
column5: It's like your own bedroom - your personal space in the house.

column4: The admin (root user)'s personal folder. Different from /home, this is only for the administrator.
column5: It's like the house owner's private room, separate from everyone else's.

column4: Holds settings and configuration files for the system and installed programs.
column5: It's like an instructions manual or settings booklet for the whole house.

column4: Basic programs everyone can use, such as ls, cp, and mv.
column5: It's like a toolbox kept in the living room that anyone in the house can use.

column4: Programs mainly used by the admin, such as reboot and shutdown.
column5: It's like a toolbox kept in a locked cupboard, only for the owner.

column4: Contains most installed apps, libraries, and documentation - similar to Program Files in Windows.
column5: It's like a big storeroom holding most of the household appliances.

column4: Holds data that keeps changing, such as logs, mail, and website files.
column5: It's like a diary that gets new entries added every single day.

column4: Stores temporary files that can be safely deleted anytime, especially after a restart.
column5: It's like a trash bin or scratch pad for things you don't need to keep.

column4: Holds extra or third-party software that isn't part of the base system.
column5: It's like a guest room used for extra furniture that doesn't belong elsewhere.

column4: Represents hardware like hard disks, USB drives, and printers as if they were files.
column5: It's like the switchboard connecting all electrical appliances in the house.

column4: A virtual folder showing live info about running processes and the kernel - it doesn't really exist on disk.
column5: It's like a live CCTV screen showing what's happening in the house right now.

column4: A virtual folder exposing details about the kernel, hardware, and device drivers.
column5: It's like a control panel showing the technical wiring details of the house.
